- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.8), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes; apply a 1–3 day lag correction: if price spiked 3+ days ago, reduce forecast by 1–2%.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overshoots in early periods (first 5–7 days); cap forecast at +5% above recent 7-day average to avoid overconfidence.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.8 within 3 days), model fails to adjust; apply a 2–5 day smoothing filter to avoid abrupt reversals.
